title: Two family trees
hook: one wedding becomes four, and two families tell their whole histories first
carry: gotra: a wedding joins two family lines

segments.voice: Yesterday, Janaka's bow, part three: Rama asked first, lifted it as if in play, and it broke like thunder. Your line was lila, what crushes kings is God's play.

Janaka's messengers ride hard to Ayodhya. They stand before Dasharatha, the king who not long ago begged a sage not to take his young son. Your Rama broke Shiva's bow, they tell him. Your Lakshmana is with him, safe. King Janaka asks you to come to Mithila for the wedding. You can imagine the old man's face. The next morning Dasharatha sets out with Vasishtha, his priests, his army and his treasure. When the two kings meet, Janaka welcomes him like family before they are family.
screen: `MESSENGERS RIDE TO AYODHYA.` → `YOUR RAMA BROKE SHIVA'S BOW.` → `TWO KINGS EMBRACE.`

segments.voice: Before anyone marries, the families recite their family trees, aloud, all the way back. Vasishtha names the line of Ikshvaku, generation after generation: from Brahma, through Manu, Ikshvaku himself, kings like Sagara, whose sons dug deep into the earth, and Bhagiratha, who brought the Ganga down from heaven, all the way to Dasharatha. Then Janaka names his own line from King Nimi down, including Devarata, who received the bow. Why? Because in Hindu teaching vivaha, marriage, is a samskara, one of the sacred rites that mark a life, and it doesn't join two people only. It joins two lines. Hindu families still do this. Many know their gotra, the family line traced back to an ancient sage, a rishi, like Vasishtha himself or Bharadvaja. At many weddings the priest calls out both families' gotras and ancestors before the vows. Then Janaka makes the formal gift: Sita to Rama, and his second daughter, Urmila, to Lakshmana. And then a lovely thing happens. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha together suggest something more. Janaka's younger brother, Kushadhvaja, has two daughters too, Mandavi and Shrutakirti. Why not give them to Bharata and Shatrughna? Janaka agrees with joy. So one wedding becomes four: four brothers, four brides, two royal houses woven together in a single day. Before the ceremony, Dasharatha gives away an enormous gift of cows in his sons' names. From now on, whatever happens in Ayodhya happens to Mithila too.
screen: `THE FAMILY TREES, ALOUD.` · `VIVAHA: A SAMSKARA.` · `GOTRA: A LINE BACK TO A SAGE.` · `ONE WEDDING BECOMES FOUR.` · then, large: `TWO HOUSES, ONE DAY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the people who came before you, parents or the ones who raised you, grandparents, names you know and names you don't, and feel the line of them stretching back and ending here, in this breath. If you know your family's gotra or home village, say it quietly. If you pray, you can remember them in your own way.
Vivaha, the wedding rite. Rama and Sita, Lakshmana and Urmila, Bharata and Mandavi, Shatrughna and Shrutakirti: two royal houses joined in one day.
Your line: gotra, a wedding joins two family lines. Two long family stories, joined in a single day. Until tomorrow.
